fixed.item: breakages.json row 1 (T-7d4006bda247ba-01, the only failing authored spec, seeds 0 and 41 'damage'): the iron upright on its heel rest scorched the ironing board through manipulation's legacy contact-heat block, which asked no phys.contact_heat hook
fixed.how: handling.hot_contact (called from after_placement while the contact_heat law is deferred) computes the law's severity min(1, (T - limit) / thermal.CONTACT_SPAN_K) and returns before marking when phys.thermal.contact_claimed(w, eid, sid, temp, severity) is true, exactly as thermal.contact_check does; unclaimed contacts scorch as before.
fixed.test: tests/test_manipulation.py PhaseOneFinishTests.test_the_legacy_contact_heat_rule_asks_every_contact_heat_hook_first (law deferred and active; the claim gets the law's severity; fails on HEAD). T-7d4006bda247ba-01 PASS 5/5 in own mode (it was 3/5).

fixed.item: breakages.json row 2 (stack law readiness, D1): stacking.stack_reason compared the members' bounding boxes (a mixing bowl on a kitchen scale's platform was 'much larger' here, stable for the kernel)
fixed.how: stack_reason now takes the first member phys.statics.stack_verdict topples on the kernel's stack_chain and names the verdict's own rule at that member (_member_rule: contact_wd of the member against top_wd of the support, nesting by the kernel's dims, the low-flat-base exception, the centre offset with the 'reaches past it' condition; else the shelf gap or slenderness); None exactly when the verdict topples nothing; this domain's open-contents rule first because it is what settle_stack topples. Stack readiness: tests/test_manipulation.py green with the stack law forced, alone and with every ready law.
fixed.test: PhaseOneFinishTests.test_stack_reason_judges_each_member_as_the_kernels_stack_verdict_does (five stacks incl. bowl on a scale's platform, oversize, off-centre, a small offset, a slender stack; the stack verb rests the bowl on the scale with the law deferred and active; fails on HEAD)

fixed.item: breakages.json row 3 (wind law readiness): light items with wind_lift_mps lifted at 1/0.6 of the wind they need, because manipulation compared the field with the weather's 10 m wind while the kernel reads it as the speed at the item
fixed.how: world._wind_at = phys.environment.object_wind_mps(state, eid)[1] for every light item and laid-over cover (the calm cut stays the weather's wind_speed_mps < 2.5, as the kernel's environment run does); the manipulation.gust event's mps is already the speed at the items; blown_away events report the speed at the item (rounded). The idle probe is now exact about exposure (no light item or cover out in an outdoor room, free and not blown away), which keeps the system cheaper than before.
fixed.test: PhaseOneFinishTests.test_light_items_lift_at_the_wind_at_the_item (law deferred and active agree: a 4 m/s sheet stays under a 6 m/s 10 m gust, 3.6 m/s at the item, and goes at 7 m/s; indoor-only light things in a gale are idle; fails on HEAD)

fixed.item: breakages.json row 4 / red_defects 6 (wrap containment, hand-back path): unwrapping a contained broken glass on the floor only set shattered: no floor hazard, no shards
fixed.how: common.end_containment(w, eid, by) calls the kernel's impact.uncontained (shattered, the sharp floor hazard on a floor, the phys.uncontained hooks that safety answers with its shard field; idempotent) and forgets the id; unwrap and tear (packaging film) call it with by='robot'; manipulation.breaks (reveal_breaks) calls it for a wrap another domain removes (kernel attribution). The phys.broke hook now remembers every contained shattering break (opaque or see-through wrap, packaging: impact.contained), and the breaks idle probe is exact (idle while each remembered break is still broken and contained). unwrap also accepts another domain's plain wrapped: true (it crashed on True.get).
fixed.test: PhaseOneFinishTests.test_unwrapping_a_contained_break_lets_its_pieces_out (newspaper and bubble wrap unwrapped, packaging torn off, wrap removed by another domain: shattered + sharp floor hazard, phys.uncontained hook exactly once, nothing left pending; fails on HEAD). With all domains loaded the safety domain now scatters 17 shards (probe).

fixed.item: breakages.json row 5 / red_defects 8 (lift monotonicity on damp or wet surfaces): a damp item slipped one-handed from 4.8 kg while the same item at 8.01 kg was held with two hands (the adaptive one-hand cap was the rated dry squeeze)
fixed.how: common.grip_outcome: for a one-hand normal/handle grip not supported, cap = min(body.grip_limit_n, max(mode cap, rated_squeeze_n, 1.3 x required)): the adaptive squeeze rises to the hardware limit for the surface it actually grips; only a surface that 150 N cannot hold slips (oily or soapy from about 3 kg), monotonically in mass. A squeeze raised on a slippery fragile item can crack it (the test's 0.9 kg oily glass bottle now cracks in the hand instead of slipping; it breaks either way unless supported from below).
fixed.test: GraspTests.test_lift_monotonicity_a_one_hand_lift_never_slips_on_mass_alone (six damp/wet cases x ten masses 0.5-10 kg all held; oily and soapy monotone; fails on HEAD), GraspTests.test_oily_bottle_breaks_or_slips_unless_supported (renamed from test_oily_bottle_slips_unless_supported: the bottle breaks, a 4 kg oily cast-iron pan slips, both held from below)

fixed.how: common.coil_of / common.roll_of read every owner's shape (dict -> dict, True or a coiling word -> {}, electrical's 'uncoiled', False, None -> None); velcro/unvelcro note secured/strapped only in this domain's dicts and leave another owner's value as written (the strap is the velcro record); uncoil (roll unroll=true), the manipulation.deploy_test event and drapes() go through coil_of (they crashed or misread the same way; a laid-out 'uncoiled' cord now drapes like any long cord).
fixed.test: PhaseOneFinishTests.test_velcro_and_coils_accept_every_owners_coiled_and_rolled_field (bool, word and rolled true: velcro/unvelcro/uncoil without a crash and the owner's value untouched; 'uncoiled' is not coiled; this domain's dict notes secured; deploy test on a bool coil; fails on HEAD). requests.request: Lift plan on slippery surfaces (residual of red_defects 8): house_sim/kernel/phys/forces.lift_plan gives one hand any item up to the hand's rating, but on an oily or soapy surface no hand can hold more than about 2-3 kg by friction even at body.grip_limit_n (150 N), so a 3-8 kg oily item slips one-handed while an 8.01 kg one goes two-handed (cradled) and is held.
